sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (c_x, c_y, ell) in F_64^3 anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f_c(z) = z^2 + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K_Kolm <= 192 + c_0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds. Across magnifications zeta in [10^0, 10^8], C^1 Fourier and lattice-noise bases collapse to post-standardization rank ~2.25 and SHA-256 PRNG exhibits avalanche discontinuity (rho ~ 0.019, 50.6% micro-step retention), whereas dM uniquely sustains both rank (~10.0) and local continuity (rho in [0.81, 0.97], 89.2% retention). Under leak-free 10-fold CV across four zero-scaler-byte non-linear benchmarks, FNS with an INT8 readout surpasses 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 pp while delivering 10.7x-129x total Flash reduction (725x-2,773x hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs (90.30% Ionosphere in 285 B; 97.22% Optical Digits in 2,598 B; 97.90% PenDigits in 2,598 B; 87.00% Satimage in 1,570 B).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Modern neural networks achieve strong empirical generalization by storing every synaptic weight as an explicit numerical scalar in dense tensor arrays [1], incurring linear O(W ) persistent memory growth in the total scalar parameter count . While manageable on datacenter accelerators, this linear footprint creates severe non-volatile Flash bottleneck on resource-constrained edge microcontrollers, embedded telemetry nodes, and autonomous sensors where on-chip Flash ROM is tightly bounded (32256 KB) and static memory reads dominate system energy [2, 3]. Compression techniquesincluding post-training quantization, 1.58-bit ternary models [4], sparse subnetwork pruning [5], structured kernel transforms [6], and hash-bucket weight sharing [7]reduce the constant bit prefactor per weight, yet retain O(W ) or O(Bhash) persistent storage scaling. Biological nervous systems adopt contrasting developmental strategy: compact genomic encodings orchestrate far more synaptic junctions than explicit point-by-point storage could accommodate by relying on recursive, selfsimilar morphogenetic rules. In one-dimensional complex dynamics, the connectedness locus of the monic quadratic family fc(z) = z2 + [811] offers an analytic extreme of procedural structure: lookup-free recurrence generates non-rectifiable bifurcation boundary whose local Hausdorff dimension is dimH (M ) = 2 for every open set intersecting [12]. In this paper, we formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), procedural weight derivation framework that replaces explicit hiddenlayer storage with constant 24-byte IEEE-754 Float64 coordinate seed Θ = (cx, cy, ℓ) F3 anchored near M. 64 Consistent with fundamental Shannon and Kolmogorov information limits [13, 14], we do not claim to compress arbitrary high-entropy frontier language models into 24 B. Rather, we address three concrete representation-learning and TinyML systems questions: (i) Under leak-free evaluation on genuinely non-linear, zero-scaler-byte real-world benchmarks, how does FNS compare against quantized linear classifiers, seeded-PRNG random features, hashed reservoirs, and converged quantized MLPs? (ii) What measurable structural properties separate from cryp1 tographic PRNGs, smooth Fourier sums, and fixed-lattice value noise? (iii) How do geometric sampling apertures and gradient-free optimizers govern spectral conditioning and zero-readout synthesis? Building substantially upon our preliminary archive [15] (which evaluated only 2D synthetic tasks on uniform grid), this work makes five contributions: 1. Smooth Boundary Kernel & Multi-Scale Generator Ablation: We formulate large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape-time kernel and evaluate against SHA-256 PRNG, smooth 2D Fourier bases, and fixed-lattice value noise across eight magnification decades (ζ = 10ℓ, ℓ {0, . . . , 8}). We demonstrate empirically that smooth 1 generators collapse after standardization to an effective matrix rank of 2.25 (verifying planar Taylor-ramp rank bound), whereas SHA-256 PRNG exhibits complete cryptographic avalanche (ρ 0.019, collapsing to 50.60% accuracy under 1% micro-step). By contrast, uniquely combines sustained post-standardization rank ( 10.0), local continuity (ρ [0.81, 0.97]), and 89.15% micro-step stability with zero lookup tables. 2. Four Geometric Sampling Apertures: We formalize and compare four zero-overhead coordinate stencilsa baseline Cartesian Grid, 3 3 Ruleof-Thirds nodal stencil aligned with Z/9Z modular residue indexing and dynamically coprime sub-strides, an area-preserving ϕ-Vogel phyllotaxis spiral [16], and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod ({0.60, 1.00, 1.60} zoom cascade)showing statistically significant accuracy improvements (p 0.023 on UCI PenDigits) and up to +25.5% relative spectral rank utilization gains at zero additional persistent storage. 3. Zero-Scaler-Byte Non-Linear Benchmarks & Fair Baselines: Using four genuinely non-linear realworld benchmarks requiring 0 of feature-scaler persistence (UCI Ionosphere, Optical Digits, PenDigits, and Statlog Satimage) under unified 10-fold stratified cross-validation, we benchmark FNS transparently against 0-hidden Linear-INT8, 8-byte Seeded-PRNG RFF/ELM, fixed 2D SplitMix64 Hashed-ELM, and converged FP32/INT8/INT4 MLPs with exact layerwise scale accounting. 4. Information-Theoretic Capacity Bounds & Equal-Budget ES Scaling: We prove conditional Kolmogorov complexity (KKolm(W, d, H) 192 + c0 bits) and Shannon entropy bounds (H(W, b) 192 bits) delineating FNSs System-1 operating regime, and evaluate four equal-budget (32 evals/gen) zeroreadout multi-patch optimizers, including Hybrid Elitist + Rank-1 ES inspired by EGGROLL [17]. 5. Warmed-Up Boot Synthesis & Apples-toApples SRAM Profiling: We quantify monotonic boot-time synthesis latency (8.0523.29 ms) against 2 identical pure-NumPy single-sample (13.621.0 µs) and batch (5.68.4 µs) SRAM inference, demonstrating parity with dense MLP forward-pass FLOPs once materialized in volatile memory.

sections.title: Positioning
sections.content: Procedural weight derivation intersects five established research lines, summarized in Table 1. Indirect Encodings and Hypernetworks. Compositional Pattern Producing Networks (CPPNs) and HyperNEAT [18] generate spatial connectivity matrices by querying an evolved coordinate neural network, while HyperNetworks [19] train an auxiliary network to predict target weights via backpropagation. Both approaches persist learned neural generators consuming kilobytes to megabytes. FractalNet [20] employs self-similar macrorouting without residual connections, but trains and stores all tensor weights explicitly. FNS eliminates learned generator parameters entirely via lookup-free complex quadratic recurrence. Random Features, ELMs, Fastfood, and Hashed Reservoirs. Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) [21, 22] and Random Fourier Features (RFF) [23,24] pair fixed nonlinear hidden projections with closed-form L2-regularized linear readouts. Fastfood [6] compresses explicit Gaussian projections from O(dH) to O(H) storage via structured WalshHadamard transforms, while HashedNets [7] hash weights into Bhash shared buckets with sign hashing during backpropagation. Importantly, fixed ELM/RFF hidden layers can themselves be regenerated at boot from an 8-byte PRNG seed (O(1) Flash). We therefore explicitly include 8-byte Seeded-PRNG RFF and ELM alongside explicit RFF and untrained 2D Hashed-ELM in Section 5.5, isolating the exact trade-offs between PRNG reservoirs and continuous boundary synthesis. Implicit Representations and TinyML Compression. Periodic implicit neural representations such as SIREN [25] compress continuous signals into network weights, operating in the dual direction of FNS. In TinyML, MCUNet [2], Lottery Ticket sparse subnetworks [5], and 1.58-bit ternary weights [4] push explicit weight footprints toward sub-byte precision while retaining O(W ) asymptotic Flash scaling. Intrinsic Dimensionality and Backprop-Free Evolution. Li et al. [26] showed that many learning objectives possess compact intrinsic dimensions. Black-box Evolution Strategies (OpenES) [27] and recent hyperscale rank-r perturbation schemes such as EGGROLL [17] remove backpropagation entirely by averaging parallel low-rank perturbations, enabling pure-integer and non-differentiable training. sections.title: 7 Limitations, Epistemic Scope,
sections.content: and Future Directions Explicitly bounding where FNS is not optimal guides disciplined adoption: 1. Information-Theoretic Ceiling: By Proposition 1, each 24-byte seed conveys at most 192 bits of conditional information. FNS is suited to compact System-1 classifiers, edge controllers, and deterministic guardrails rather than replacing high-entropy frontier transformers. 2. Readout and Feature-Scaler Storage: Mode II shifts Flash scaling from O(dH + HC) to O(1 + HC), which dominates total Flash when is large (2,574 readout vs. 24 hidden on 10-class digits at = 256). Furthermore, datasets lacking fixed input bounds require storing per-feature scaling statistics (8d FP32) that dense MLPs can fold into W1, whereas FNS must persist them unless raw or constant-scaled inputs are used. 3. Mode II Parity with Seeded-PRNG Reservoirs: When hidden seeds are unoptimized, 8-byte counterbased PRNG RFF/ELM reservoirs achieve slightly higher accuracy on Optical Digits and PenDigits in 16 less Flash. Future Mode II work should investigate inner-fold coordinate optimization of Θ along to test whether boundary continuity unlocks dataadaptive reservoir gains unattainable by discontinuous PRNG seeds. 4. Curvature-Sensitive Readout Quantization & On-Target MCU Profiling: Two-Spirals INT8 degradation (91.0% 58.5%) shows that tightly wound boundaries require FP32 or mixed-precision readouts, and host-CPU Python timings must be complemented by native C/Q16.16 fixed-point benchmarking on physical ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V microcontrollers. Broader Research Outlook. Looking beyond the compact classification benchmarks evaluated in this paper, the lookup-free boundary paradigm naturally invites four longer-horizon research directions deferred to dedicated future studies: (i) scaling pure-integer, backpropagationfree low-rank evolution strategies [17] to larger multilayer procedural architectures; (ii) low-bandwidth policy synchronization in decentralized multi-agent collec10 Figure 4: Experiment 4 Unified 10-Fold Stratified CV MemoryAccuracy Pareto Frontiers (H {32, 64, 128, 256}, 0 scaler overhead) across four non-linear real-world benchmarks. sections.title: 8 Conclusion
sections.content: We formulated and systematically evaluated Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), constant-storage procedural hidden-layer derivation architecture based on largebailout (R = 256) complex quadratic boundary dynamics and four geometric sampling apertures. Through controlled multi-scale ablations and unified 10-fold stratified cross-validation across boolean logic, 2D manifolds, and four zero-scaler-byte non-linear real-world benchmarks (d = 1664, = 210), we established three conclusions: (1) among 24-byte lookup-free generators, uniquely combines scale-free post-standardization matrix rank ( 10.0 across ζ [100, 108], vs. 2.25 for 1 Taylor-flattened Fourier/lattice bases) with smooth local continuity (ρ [0.81, 0.97], retaining 89.15% accuracy under 1% micro-steps vs. 50.60% for SHA-256 PRNG); (2) coprime 3 3 Rule-of-Thirds and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod apertures significantly improve spectral conditioning and multi-class generalization at zero storage cost; and (3) pairing 24-byte procedural hidden layer with an INT8 linear head outperforms 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 percentage points while delivering 10.7129 total Flash reduction (7252,773 hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs at matching runtime SRAM latency.
